tag: the generic handler goes, so a 500 leaves no record again
why: THE COMMITTED DEFECT, exactly as measured at HEAD: with only the RequestValidationError handler registered, an uncaught exception on any route leaves no record anywhere. 13 record_outcome call sites, a hash-chained UEG across 11 modules, psutil vitals in 8 - and nothing at all about a 500.

tag: the handler swallows the failure instead of reporting it
why: Recording a failure is not RESOLVING one. A handler that answers 200 turns every crash into a success for every caller and every rate computed downstream - strictly worse than no handler, because the record would exist while the response lied about it.

tag: the record claims a cause it does not have
why: The item says the record must never invent a cause it does not have. The handler knows the exception CLASS, the route and the time; a class name is not a diagnosis, and a record asserting the cause is established invites a reader to stop looking.

tag: the failure is not written to the outcome ledger
why: The ruling puts the record in the ledger this platform already keeps, and the surface reads that ledger by kind. A renamed kind is silent: the row exists and nothing finds it, which is the reach class this plan keeps catching one step short of a module nothing imports.

tag: an empty ledger reads the same as a clean one
why: THE CLAUSE THIS ITEM TURNS ON. No failures over a POPULATED ledger says recording works and nothing broke; no failures over an EMPTY one says nothing about reliability whatsoever. Collapsing them shows the absence of any statement as health, which is the untruth the item was written against.

tag: the page stops distinguishing the empty case
why: The route can report three states and the SURFACE is where a person reads them. W503's class, so the leg asserts the literal with its quotes rather than the field name, which survives a disabled branch.

tag: a pin this item explicitly excludes is removed
why: HALF THE RULING RESTED ON A FALSE PREMISE and the item says so: pip show reports this Required-by chromadb, which agentic_core/ai/ceo/memory_v01.py imports on the cross-request recall path, and requirements.txt is a 298-line LOCK that lists transitive dependencies by design. Removing one breaks the install rather than tidying it, so the item excludes the retirement and the manifest question is a separate row with its own measurement.
